phases.title: M0 - Runnable foundation
phases.description: Local browser/API/database and PDS fixtures run reproducibly; staging infrastructure and resumable deployment intent are ready.

phases.title: M1 - Private deployment alpha
phases.description: An invited owner deploys a real managed-domain PDS, creates an account, verifies federation and configures a BYO handle.

phases.title: M2 - Recoverable managed service
phases.description: Identity custody, full restores, monitoring, safe upgrades, tenant isolation and operator suspension are demonstrated.

phases.title: M3 - Paid pilot
phases.description: Subscription entitlements, usage limits, fleet capacity, exports and support workflows operate through a measured invited pilot.

phases.title: M4 - Public launch
phases.description: Browser onboarding and independent production infrastructure pass the documented release gate before public signup opens.

phases.title: M5 - Additional access and portability
phases.description: Optional CLI, custom PDS endpoints, account migration and organization collaboration extend the qualified API.

labels.name: ready-for-agent

labels.name: priority: P2

issues.title: Run the standalone local stack and CI smoke journey
issues.build: A contributor can start a Go management API, React interface and disposable PostgreSQL, then open the interface and see database-backed service readiness.
criteria: Document and pin supported toolchains, dependency locks and local startup commands.
A versioned migration initializes the management schema; incompatible schema versions fail clearly.
The browser calls the API and displays readiness without exposing configuration secrets.
Gitea CI builds both applications and runs a clean-database smoke journey without cloud credentials.
issues.verification: Start from a clean checkout, open the browser, stop PostgreSQL and verify readiness changes; run the same build and smoke gates in CI.
issues.boundary: No deployment, billing, existing application imports, production cloud creation or live mail is needed.
issues.body_template:
<!-- pds-ass-roadmap:01 -->

## What to build

A contributor can start a Go management API, React interface and disposable PostgreSQL, then open the interface and see database-backed service readiness.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document and pin supported toolchains, dependency locks and local startup commands.
- [ ] A versioned migration initializes the management schema; incompatible schema versions fail clearly.
- [ ] The browser calls the API and displays readiness without exposing configuration secrets.
- [ ] Gitea CI builds both applications and runs a clean-database smoke journey without cloud credentials.

## Verification

Start from a clean checkout, open the browser, stop PostgreSQL and verify readiness changes; run the same build and smoke gates in CI.

## Blocked by

{{BLOCKERS}}

## Boundaries

No deployment, billing, existing application imports, production cloud creation or live mail is needed.

## Planning reference

Phase: M0 - Runnable foundation. Priority: P0.
[Implementation plan](https://git.subcult.tv/PatrickFanella/pds-ass/src/branch/main/docs/implementation-plan.md) and [roadmap](https://git.subcult.tv/PatrickFanella/pds-ass/src/branch/main/docs/roadmap.md).

issues.title: Sign in and create an owner-scoped organization
issues.build: A customer signs in through configured OIDC, creates an organization and sees only that organization in the browser.
criteria: Choose and document the production OIDC provider; local tests use an isolated test issuer.
Validate state, nonce, issuer, audience and callback destinations; browser sessions use secure cookie settings.
Identity keys use issuer and subject; matching email or DID never merges users.
Organization ownership gates API access, and sign-out/revocation invalidates management sessions.
Two owners cannot enumerate or modify each other's organization.
issues.verification: Exercise successful login, rejected callback replay, wrong issuer/audience, logout and cross-organization access through browser and API tests.
issues.boundary: Management identity is independent of PDS login; multi-member organization roles are a later extension.

issues.title: Bootstrap and register a staging hosting node
issues.build: An operator creates a staging node from versioned infrastructure configuration and sees its verified identity and usable capacity in management inventory.
criteria: Record provider, region, spend ceiling, management/PDS domains and backup destination before provisioning.
OpenTofu creates only declared resources; Ansible configures Ubuntu, Docker, private administration, firewall and a restricted agent.
Only HTTPS/required certificate validation is public; database and host administration remain private.
Node enrollment validates a one-time bootstrap credential and authenticates subsequent agent connections.
Infrastructure state and bootstrap secrets are protected; rerunning configuration does not create duplicate nodes.
issues.verification: Review the infrastructure plan, bootstrap an authorized staging node, register it and rerun convergence; reject an unknown or replayed node enrollment.
issues.boundary: This issue establishes one provider and region; executing paid provisioning requires actual account credentials and an approved budget.
issues.body_template:
<!-- pds-ass-roadmap:03 -->

## What to build

An operator creates a staging node from versioned infrastructure configuration and sees its verified identity and usable capacity in management inventory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record provider, region, spend ceiling, management/PDS domains and backup destination before provisioning.
- [ ] OpenTofu creates only declared resources; Ansible configures Ubuntu, Docker, private administration, firewall and a restricted agent.
- [ ] Only HTTPS/required certificate validation is public; database and host administration remain private.
- [ ] Node enrollment validates a one-time bootstrap credential and authenticates subsequent agent connections.
- [ ] Infrastructure state and bootstrap secrets are protected; rerunning configuration does not create duplicate nodes.

## Verification

Review the infrastructure plan, bootstrap an authorized staging node, register it and rerun convergence; reject an unknown or replayed node enrollment.

## Blocked by

{{BLOCKERS}}

## Boundaries

This issue establishes one provider and region; executing paid provisioning requires actual account credentials and an approved budget.

issues.title: Qualify a disposable official PDS runtime
issues.build: An operator launches a disposable pinned PDS runtime with separate database and blob storage, then verifies its supported protocol and transport behavior.
criteria: Pin the official PDS image by digest and render a reusable runtime manifest.
Allocate separate PDS SQLite state, blob namespace and credentials; persist them across a restart.
Retain invite codes and repository rate limits; define CPU, memory, disk and account limits.
Health and WebSocket checks run through a test ingress; database and storage failures report accurately.
Document isolated identity fixtures and a separate designated live-account qualification path.
issues.verification: Run a disposable runtime, restart it, test storage and WebSockets, and prove expected data persists; no production identity is created in CI.
issues.boundary: Keep the upstream protocol implementation; do not replace SQLite or rewrite PDS functionality.
issues.body_template:
<!-- pds-ass-roadmap:04 -->

## What to build

An operator launches a disposable pinned PDS runtime with separate database and blob storage, then verifies its supported protocol and transport behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pin the official PDS image by digest and render a reusable runtime manifest.
- [ ] Allocate separate PDS SQLite state, blob namespace and credentials; persist them across a restart.
- [ ] Retain invite codes and repository rate limits; define CPU, memory, disk and account limits.
- [ ] Health and WebSocket checks run through a test ingress; database and storage failures report accurately.
- [ ] Document isolated identity fixtures and a separate designated live-account qualification path.

## Verification

Run a disposable runtime, restart it, test storage and WebSockets, and prove expected data persists; no production identity is created in CI.

## Blocked by

{{BLOCKERS}}

## Boundaries

Keep the upstream protocol implementation; do not replace SQLite or rewrite PDS functionality.

issues.title: Submit and resume a durable deployment request
issues.build: An owner names a server in the browser, submits a deployment request and can return later to the same durable operation and progress history.
criteria: Persist deployment intent and a River job in one PostgreSQL transaction.
Validate name, supported region and organization-scoped idempotency key.
A test provisioner exercises queued/configuring/checking/ready/failed states and bounded retries.
Closing the browser or restarting the worker does not lose progress or create another instance.
Errors are customer-readable and secret-free; only authorized owners can read operation status.
issues.verification: Replay an identical request, conflict on different parameters, crash the test worker and reopen the browser; verify one intent and one resulting instance.
issues.boundary: This slice uses a test provisioner; real host execution follows without changing the customer contract.

issues.title: Provision a real PDS through the restricted host agent
issues.build: An invited owner requests a deployment and the worker starts one PDS on a registered staging node, preserving the instance after worker retries.
criteria: Placement reserves measured host capacity and an instance-specific persistent volume/storage namespace.
Worker and agent use authenticated private communication and an allowlisted lifecycle contract.
Neither public API nor customer runtime receives host Docker administration, provider credentials or arbitrary execution capability.
A crash after container creation reconciles by stable instance ID before retrying.
Exhausted capacity, agent timeout and uncertain completion leave diagnosable state without deleting user data.
issues.verification: Deploy to staging, interrupt the worker after host success, retry and verify exactly one runtime/volume; reject unregistered agents and arbitrary image/path requests.
issues.boundary: Deploy only pinned service-managed PDS runtimes; no customer code hosting or per-request VM installation.

issues.title: Expose stable managed PDS hostnames with HTTPS
issues.build: A customer receives a stable provider-managed PDS URL with valid HTTPS and working protocol/WebSocket routing.
criteria: Use a registered PDS domain separate from management/OAuth application domains.
Automate supported DNS and Caddy configuration for endpoints and required account-handle hostnames.
Issue certificates only for verified service inventory; reject unknown hosts and conflicting names.
Handle certificate/DNS failures as explicit progress or failure states rather than marking the server ready.
Record endpoint identity independently from node placement so recovery can retain the hostname.
issues.verification: Reach a staging PDS through its public URL, validate TLS and WebSockets, reject an unregistered hostname, and retry a failed certificate step.
issues.boundary: Managed hostnames are the default; customer-owned PDS endpoints are a later issue.

issues.title: Guide the owner through first-account enrollment
issues.build: After deployment, the owner follows a scoped enrollment flow to create and verify the first AT account on their PDS and log in with a compatible client.
criteria: Issue an expiring, tenant-scoped enrollment invitation and prevent reuse.

issues.verification: Complete enrollment and login on a designated staging identity; test wrong tenant, reused invitation, expired invitation and mail failure without creating extra accounts.
issues.boundary: Fresh accounts only; existing-account migration and delegated organization publishing are separate work.

issues.title: Prove signed records, media and downstream federation
issues.build: The customer can authenticate, write and read a signed record and media on the hosted PDS; the service distinguishes local readiness from downstream indexing.
criteria: Verify DID/handle/PDS resolution, repository write/read and referenced blob retrieval on a designated identity.

issues.boundary: Hosting does not promise guaranteed Bluesky visibility, immediate indexing, or exemption from downstream policies.

issues.title: Protect credentials and prove identity-key recovery
issues.build: An operator can securely provision runtime credentials and recover a disposable account's identity from independently protected recovery material.
criteria: Choose the supported runtime encryption/KMS and recovery-custody approach before paid customer use.
Separate tenant credentials, provider tokens, PLC rotation material and recovery-key access.
Store references rather than secret values in jobs, logs, browser responses, exports and audit records.
Rehearse key recovery and credential rotation with protected backups; identify unrecoverable conditions honestly.
Capture administrative access/rotation evidence without revealing key material.
issues.verification: Scan artifacts and logs for leaked values, rotate designated staging credentials and recover identity with the documented recovery path.
issues.boundary: SOPS configuration encryption alone is not a full identity recovery plan; customer-held keys are opt-in and require a supported custody flow.

issues.title: Back up and restore a complete customer PDS
issues.build: An operator restores a populated customer PDS onto a clean node, retaining its identity, hostname, repositories, media and necessary private preferences.
criteria: Back up all PDS-wide and account SQLite databases using a consistent SQLite-aware method, plus protected configuration and referenced blob inventory.
Use independent recovery storage with separate access credentials and retention metadata.
Restore to a fresh node with fencing that prevents two active writers under the same endpoint.
Compare database/repository/blob inventories and authenticate/write again after restoration.
Measure achieved data-loss and recovery intervals against the proposed 15-minute/60-minute pilot targets; expose gaps rather than promising them.
issues.verification: Populate a disposable PDS, simulate node loss, restore it, compare inventories and prove new writes and downstream events with the original identity.
issues.boundary: A volume snapshot or account CAR export alone does not complete disaster recovery; retain the old copy until the restored instance is verified.

issues.build: After management database loss, an operator restores organizations and operations and reconnects them to live host inventory without duplicating PDS deployments.

Handle ambiguous/orphaned resources as operator work rather than deleting or duplicating them.

issues.verification: Restore a disposable management database while a host runtime exists and a job has an uncertain outcome; verify that resumption allocates no duplicate.
issues.boundary: Control-plane recovery does not replace PDS data recovery, and billing processor state requires separate reconciliation.

issues.title: Detect outages, failed backups and exhausted capacity
issues.build: An operator receives actionable alerts for PDS availability, certificate/storage problems, job backlog and stale recovery evidence.
criteria: Collect bounded tenant/node metrics and structured logs without account passwords, keys or private records.
Use an external HTTPS/WebSocket probe that can detect failure of the hosting network itself.
Alert on disk/storage thresholds, exhausted placement capacity, stale backups, restore failure and queued/failed operations.

issues.verification: Inject endpoint, disk, queue and backup failures and verify the intended alert and operator runbook; verify no sensitive payload enters monitoring.
issues.boundary: Monitoring must work when the application is down; no uptime/SLA claim is inferred from installing dashboards.

issues.title: Upgrade a PDS with staged rollout and safe recovery
issues.build: An operator qualifies a new PDS image on a populated staging instance, upgrades one selected tenant and either verifies it or follows a compatible recovery path.
criteria: Pin release images and record before/after runtime and schema versions.
Create and validate a recovery checkpoint before a potentially incompatible upgrade.

- [ ] Check post-switch auth, record/blob inventory, signing and downstream identity resolution.
- [ ] Document failure/rollback boundaries and confirm state held outside the PDS; never claim a universal automatic rollback after identity mutation.

## Verification

Rehearse inbound and outbound migration between designated populated test hosts; interrupt transfers and inject missing blobs/stale identity resolution.

Real-account migration requires its owner's authorization; complex/adversarial recovery and guaranteed completion times are separate qualifications.
